items.proposed_content: The span packages the all-real-zero regime as Laguerre–Pólya membership and, using the even entire-function structure, positive value at the origin, and Hadamard factorization, represents H_t by a product whose zeros have reciprocal-square summability. This representation gains a convergent zero-indexed description while retaining the entire function as the global object; it does not locate the threshold, certify a close pair, or supply the derivative and zero-motion machinery used elsewhere. The class formula and exact product factors remain unsafe without scan verification.

items.proposed_content: Matching the quadratic coefficient of the t=0 Hadamard product with the even Taylor expansion of H_0 identifies the total reciprocal-square sum over its zeros with a ratio of low-order Fourier-kernel moments. The operation compresses an infinite zero set into one aggregate fixed-time identity and lets cited moment computations evaluate that aggregate, but it neither locates individual zeros nor establishes a quantity conserved across t. Any numerical value, precision claim, or formula-exact use still depends on the external moment table and scan verification.

items.proposed_content: Theorem 1 turns one certified Lehmer-pair statistic into a scalar constraint on the de Bruijn–Newman threshold: a negative environmental term gives a positive-threshold conclusion, while a positive environmental term yields an explicit negative pair-derived lower bound. Corollary 1 then applies a separate limiting step: under an infinite family of positive-environment Lehmer pairs whose gaps shrink to zero, the lower bounds accumulate at zero and force only the one-sided conclusion that the threshold is nonnegative. The scalar compression makes local certificates directly comparable with a global threshold, but the span does not supply the later collision proof or establish that the required infinite family exists; equality at zero remains compatible with the Riemann Hypothesis.

items.proposed_content: Applying the established pair-to-threshold map to the high-index Lehmer certificate produces the paper’s sharper negative lower bound. Comparing the more precise bound with the leading negative squared-gap term shows that this certificate’s result is only weakly affected by the environmental estimate, which supports a search heuristic favoring exceptionally close pairs that can also be certified. The closing outlook is incremental: further extended zero calculations may supply improved bounds; this span does not prove infinitely many Lehmer pairs, convergence of the bounds to zero, or the Riemann Hypothesis. Exact values and signs remain unsafe without the scan.

items.proposed_content: The proof normalizes each certified squared gap together with its positive environmental term into a parameter lying in a fixed interval, then expresses the pair-derived threshold bound through a monotone scalar function of that parameter. This removes irrelevant scale and transfers the shrinking-gap limit to the lower-bound limit: under the stated infinite Lehmer-pair hypotheses, the bounds approach zero, and because every one is below the global threshold, they force the one-sided result that the threshold is nonnegative. The argument neither identifies the threshold with zero nor produces the infinite certified family, and its exact normalization is unsafe without the scan.

items.proposed_content: Multiplicity is a local boundary event for the real-zero phase: a small backward heat-time perturbation of a multiple real zero violates a necessary Laguerre–Pólya inequality, while a small forward perturbation of a nondegenerate double zero creates two nearby simple real zeros. Together with the threshold characterization and the higher-multiplicity reduction, these one-sided behaviors yield simplicity of every zero strictly above the threshold.
